structured_picker.description: Ask the user to choose from 1 to 4 labelled options, with a free-text 'Other'. Used by setup and reconfigure for persona and industry selection.

file_read.description: Read files from the harness folder.

file_write.description: Create or overwrite files in the harness folder (workspace configuration, semantic-layer lookup files, reports).

shell.description: Run a command or a short Python script. Needed only by the components that say so.

mcp:fullstory.description: Call the Fullstory analytics MCP server (metrics, segments, funnels, session review). Without it the analysis components cannot read the org.

claude-code.basis: in daily use; picker, read and write tool names are cited from shipped files: AskUserQuestion and the Write tool in .claude/commands/setup.md, the Read tool in .claude/commands/hypothesis-swarm.md, and discover_org_context as the MCP connection check in .claude/commands/setup.md (Step 3); the shell tool name is attested by Lane Greer, not established by a shipped file; flips to tested when the SC-10 transcript is in the wave folder

shell.statement: In Claude Code, the tool that runs shell commands is named Bash.

cowork.basis: One observed Cowork session on 2026-10-28 (setup run three times) showed the shell reaching local paths through device_bash, device_list_dir and device_request_folder_access, with the user granting access to each folder. That is one run, so the row stays untested. The picker (AskUserQuestion) was also used in that run, but one use does not establish it, so structured_picker stays unknown. mcp:fullstory is established by vendor documentation. Source: Claude Help Center, Get started with Claude Cowork: connectors are controlled via the Customize > Connectors page. The value is the documented way to connect an MCP server, not a tool this harness calls, and the documentation does not say the Fullstory server connects here. Detail and grades in runtime-research-20261022.md

components.job: First-time workspace setup: ask the user's analyst role and industry, copy the matching pre-built rail cells into the workspace, and write the workspace configuration. Must run before any analysis.
Change the saved role or industry later, without losing session memory or prior decisions.
Record what is known about the org in a short, dated file. No foundation and no layer: run this.

Re-check due foundation rows and add what an analysis found. Foundation exists: use it; run this when a row is over 30 days old or something returns nothing. Only a layer exists: keep using it as a lead, run this to carry it across.
Deprecated, use create-org-foundation; not for a new org. Map the org into lookup files.
Deprecated, use update-org-foundation; only for a layer not yet migrated. Rebuild its lookup files.
Always-active discipline for calling the Fullstory MCP: check the org foundation first, then build, confirm and compute metrics and segments rather than guessing.
Write a prompt for a Fullstory MCP agent that works on its own or with you.
Collect structured feedback when an MCP workflow ends unexpectedly or works well, extracting what is already in the conversation, and produce a report to send to the Fullstory team.
Collect structured feedback on how well the analysis was calibrated to the user's role and industry, producing a block to share with the Fullstory analyst.
Before presenting any finding, review a minimum of five representative user sessions and inspect page state, console and network errors, so counts are backed by observed behaviour.
Quantify synthetic and automated traffic on the org, separate it from real user behaviour, and show whether it distorts the experience metrics.
Compare how two or more user groups experience the property differently and produce a self-contained HTML report with a companion field guide.
Analyse where users drop out of a critical flow and why, and produce a self-contained HTML report with a companion field guide.
Find the top areas of user struggle across the property and produce a monthly one-page or slide-deck snapshot.
Prove a behaviour insight (dead click, spinner, rage burst) with a short animated clip or screenshot sequence of the session.
Investigate a data discrepancy or conflicting metrics by deploying independent agents on distinct hypotheses, rotating assignments and peer-reviewing, then reconciling.
Build a competitive playbook, integration value story or microsite from intake through content reasoning to a final deliverable.
Build a context bundle for the org: five structured markdown files, a job log and a multi-tab HTML report, from live Fullstory MCP data.
